findings.title: read_timeout is per-read; no overall deadline, so a slow-drip peer holds the call open
findings.evidence: read_timeout is set only via the Net::HTTP option, and the method has no wall-clock budget for the whole call.
findings.recommendation: Wrap each attempt in Timeout.timeout(OPEN_TIMEOUT + READ_TIMEOUT * some_factor) or track a deadline across the attempt loop so a server sending one byte per interval cannot keep the request alive indefinitely (currently worse because the retry loop multiplies it by MAX_ATTEMPTS).

findings.title: Retryable set omits common transient transport errors
findings.evidence: Only Net::OpenTimeout, Net::ReadTimeout, Errno::ECONNRESET are retried; DNS/connect churn raises SocketError, Errno::ETIMEDOUT, Errno::EHOSTUNREACH, EOFError, Net::HTTPBadResponse, which escape the rescue on attempt 1.
findings.recommendation: Extend RETRYABLE_ERRORS with SocketError, EOFError, Net::HTTPBadResponse, Errno::ETIMEDOUT, Errno::EHOSTUNREACH, Errno::EPIPE (or descendant narrowing) so the documented bounded retry of transient transport failures actually covers transient transport failures; document any deliberate exclusions.

findings.title: Non-success raise discards status/response and never retries 5xx or 429
findings.evidence: Any non-2xx (including transient 502/503/504 and 429) is turned into a plain RuntimeError built from a string, so callers cannot branch on the status code and the retry policy does not apply to server-side transient failures.
findings.recommendation: Define a dedicated HttpFetch::HttpError (or reuse Net::HTTPResponse) carrying response.code and body, and retry 429/500/502/503/504 with the same backoff; keep the raise outside the retryable rescue set as a distinct class so it is not swallowed.

findings.title: No host check: nil/empty host passes the https guard and fails deep inside Net::HTTP
findings.evidence: The guard only checks uri.is_a?(URI::HTTPS); a URI like https:// with no host still satisfies it, so uri.host is nil and the failure surfaces as a TypeError from the socket layer rather than ArgumentError.
findings.recommendation: After the scheme check, validate uri.host is a non-empty String (and reject userinfo if it should not be silently ignored) so malformed input fails fast with ArgumentError before any network call or retry/latency cost.

findings.title: Successful 204/205 responses return nil instead of a String body
findings.evidence: Net::HTTPSuccess includes HTTPNoContent and HTTPResetContent, for which Net::HTTPResponse#body is nil, so the method returns nil while returning a String for 200 with Content-Length 0.
findings.recommendation: Return response.body.to_s (or document a nil return) so callers doing string operations on the result do not hit NoMethodError on empty-body 2xx responses; add a test for 204.

findings.title: Retry bound, backoff, and https-only guard are untested
findings.evidence: The retry loop, exponential backoff, and MAX_ATTEMPTS cutoff have no accompanying test file, and no test commands were run for this change.
findings.recommendation: Add tests with an injected sleeper/stubbed Net::HTTP.start: exactly MAX_ATTEMPTS attempts then re-raise of the original error, no retry on the HTTP-status error, and ArgumentError for http:// and for a host-less https URI.
